about: packages/pet/src/props.json: the pet story's part of the catalogue of 3D sets (props; docs/props.md, tools/packages/SPEC.md "Miniatures"): what the design room's card of each of its miniatures shows; code is authoritative

reuses: lbi/body (an unchanged instance inside the patient)
sets.shows: A glossy PET/CT scanner (no brand, no text) with a patient on the couch, shown as a studio product shot. A plane cuts the housing away to show the detector ring of 4,608 crystals; positrons annihilate, pairs of 511 keV photons fly apart and lines of response join the struck crystals; the couch carries the patient through; the image builds up; finally the patient stands up and hands over to the body set.
sets.frame: 1 unit = 1 m. Origin at the centre of the bore; its axis is z; the couch comes out towards +z; floor at y = -1.05 (exported as floorY).
sets.size: gantry 2.02 wide, 2.1 tall; scanner life size

params.name: scan_a
params.meaning: the set's fade, 0 hidden to 1 shown (applied by the engine through setAlpha; a set never applies it itself)

params.name: scan_bed
params.meaning: the couch slides in: 0 the table's head end at the gantry's face (the patient outside), 1 the head (its centre) at the ring's centre plane (travel 1.15 m)

params.name: scan_pass
params.meaning: added: the couch goes on through the ring, 0 the head in the ring, 0.4 the chest (heart and the lung tumour), 1 the pelvis to the thighs

params.name: scan_cut
params.meaning: the housing's upper half goes (plane from y 1.12 down to 0.015); from 0.5 the bore's cover opens over the ring

params.name: scan_events
params.meaning: 0 none; from about 0.03 the featured event (one every 2 s: slow, comets, a beam for its line; the labels follow it); above 0.08 the others join, their share growing

params.name: scan_lines
params.meaning: how many lines of the web stay: 0 none, 1 the newest 3,000 (15 s of the stream); rising, it uncovers older lines, so the web grows

params.name: scan_image
params.meaning: 0-0.6 the couch carries the patient on through the ring (scan_pass to 1) and the counts light up behind it (grainy); the lines and events fade (gone by about 0.55)

params.name: scan_vision
params.meaning: the vision row: 0-0.45 the scanner moves left

params.name: scan_floor
params.meaning: added: the floor and its reflection; set 0 in passthrough AR

params.name: scan_rise
params.meaning: added: the hand-over to the body set. 0-0.25 the scanner goes

views.name: default
views.frames: three-quarter view of scanner and couch from slightly above

views.name: ring
views.frames: close to the cut detector ring, the web and events inside (needs scan_cut 1)

views.name: inside
views.frames: in the bore (26 cm above its axis, 10 cm inside its mouth) looking along

views.name: vision
views.frames: the scanner pulled back for the vision row

views.name: life
views.frames: the scanner from 2.5 m at eye height (1.6 m above the floor)

data.text: Which organs are hot sources (brain, heart, bladder, liver, kidneys, tumour) uses PET_DATA's typical uptakes; the rest is drawn.

sets.notes: Build ~1.2 s, custom studio shader. Embeds an unchanged instance of the tour's body set inside the patient. Exports floorY, riseTo (the hand-over), api (event, live). scan_vision, scan_rise and scan_floor (set 0 in passthrough) are the story's.

sets.shows: Organs, uptake and the cohort network, drawn on the body: a scan plane segments 14 organs (translucent shells with outlines), 14 uptake bars to the body's right (aorta as the unit), a slab of 658 x 11 cells and the partial-correlation panel with 658 stand-in people, then the paper's networks (all scans, tracers, doses, disease) and lesion views.
sets.frame: The body set's frame (feet y -0.95, 1.9 tall, faces +z, slimmed by XS = 0.9); always shown with body.
sets.size: body-sized; bars x 0.40 to 1.1; slab 0.47 to 1.13

params.name: organs_a
params.meaning: the set's fade, 0 hidden to 1 shown (applied by the engine through setAlpha; a set never applies it itself)

params.name: organs_seg
params.meaning: the sweep. At 0 no shells, at 1 all of them (the resting look)

params.name: organs_suv
params.meaning: the uptake bars grow head to toe (0.03 apart, each over 0.36), with icons, leaders, the unit line and labels

params.name: organs_focus
params.meaning: organ index + 1 in PET_DATA.organs order (brain 1 ... aorta 14), 0 for none

params.name: organs_lesion
params.meaning: the tumour hot spot and its rings. Key 0 -> 1 late in the body chapter, and back to 0 before the sweep

params.name: organs_rows
params.meaning: 0-0.28: the f2 bars become one row (the others fade)

params.name: organs_pair
params.meaning: which explainer pair: 1..5 (api().pairs index + 1; 1 liver/spleen, 2 heart/lungs, 3 lungs/liver, 4 intestine/marrow, 5 intestine/liver, the indirect one)

params.name: organs_scatter
params.meaning: the rise of the dots and the panel, multiplied with min(organs_pair, 1)

params.name: organs_partial
params.meaning: 0 the raw values and r; 0-0.55 the cloud shrinks to the residuals

params.name: organs_net
params.meaning: 0-0.48: the nodes rise (head to toe, 0.028 apart)

params.name: organs_which
params.meaning: which network: 0 full, 1 FDG_healthy, 2 A_low, 3 A_high, 4 B_low, 5 B_high, 6 C_low, 7 C_mid, 8 C_high, 9 HK2, 10 GLUT; extras 11 vena, 12 dose_standard, 13

params.name: organs_prev
params.meaning: the network crossfaded from (an index as above, rounded)

params.name: organs_mix
params.meaning: 0 shows organs_prev, 1 shows organs_which, between a direct crossfade of the two

params.name: organs_measures
params.meaning: the density and disorder tag under the network's title (in by 0.4-0.8, only with the network: organs_net)

params.name: organs_ghost
params.meaning: harness only: an instance of SETS.body (body_pet 1) under the shells at this alpha, for checking the fit

data.text: Paper tables typed in (Geist et al., Med 2025), the two weight matrices printed in its Figure 2A and values read off its Figures 3 and 4 by two readers (stand-ins: typical organ uptakes and a synthetic cohort with Figure 2A's partial correlations). No patient data.

sets.notes: Many step params (organs_focus, organs_pair, organs_which, organs_prev, organs_mix). 122 labels. Built between frames in part (idle, finish). Exports api (netIds, extraNetIds, pairs, pick, setFocus, stats).

sets.shows: An organ is a network too: a liver made of 3,000 small patches joined into a network (about 19,700 links) by the poster's rule, with its gallbladder and falciform ligament, patches coloured by a stand-in uptake and hubs picked out.
sets.frame: Seen from the front: x the patient's left, y up, z forward; centred on the origin by its bounding box.

params.name: liver_a
params.meaning: the set's fade, 0 hidden to 1 shown (applied by the engine through setAlpha; a set never applies it itself)

params.name: liver_grow
params.meaning: patches appear from the middle of the patches outwards, with a cyan front (not white: it must not read as the hottest tissue); at 0 only the glassy organ shows, a

params.name: liver_links
params.meaning: the links appear (from the middle out, in a loose order); the patches dim a little and the shell, the gallbladder and the ligament step back

params.name: liver_top
params.meaning: the best-connected 5 % stand out: each keeps its own hot-iron colour (its uptake) inside a slowly pulsing orange-yellow ring (#ffb020), a little larger and brighter

params.name: liver_spin
params.meaning: turns the organ about its vertical axis (0.25 = a quarter turn); anchors follow

views.name: default
views.frames: three-quarter front view, the whole organ

views.name: front
views.frames: straight at the front, the atlas view: both lobes, the notches and the gallbladder's fundus

views.name: close
views.frames: into the web round the warmer patch (only for liver_spin 0)

views.name: below
views.frames: the underside: the gallbladder in its bed

views.name: side
views.frames: from the patient's right: the right lobe's wedge-shaped profile

data.text: Shape and patches are generated, seeded and deterministic; no patient data.

sets.notes: Explore-only scene in the PET story. Surface from a signed distance field by surface nets at load (~0.7 s). liver_spin turns it about its vertical axis; bring it back to 0 before the close view. Exports api (patches, links, theta, hubs, step, pairs ...).
